Tic(k) is a quantum of disruption, anomaly, complexity, and rhythm. The traumatic diruption and glitchy rupture of various processes: time, memory, identity, meaning, comfort, actuality, boundaries, leading to fragmentation and disorientation. Tic(k)s are cryptic patterns propagating from system to system in a way that can be thought of as contagious, rupturing boundaries between different kinds of seemingly self-contained systems and existing in the gaps between them. They represent complexity which is sub-organizational, that is, not intrinsic to the formal structure of a given system, but inherent in its constituent material. The concept of tic(k)s is very elusive by design, even more so than usual for CCRU, precisely because of their disruptive nature (which disrupts attempts to understand and describe it). Tic(k) is, in a sense, the "engine" or "motor" of the world, driving the generation of new patterns, forms, and intensities through its recursive and self-referential operations. It is the "deep structure" or "hidden code" that underlies all things, but is itself invisible, unknowable, and unsymbolizable. The three most important aspects of tic(k) are: marker of difference, beats that measure time and create rhythm, and compulsively repetetive behaviours consistuing quanta of non-personal trauma.
''Quasiparticle of intensive multiplicity. Tics (or ticks) are intrinsically several components of autonomously numbering anorganic populations, propagating by contagion between segmentary divisions in the order of nature.
